Subject: Re: Fwd: DeepCare — High latency & errors on Hosted API for 32k context workloads (INVESTIGATION)

Quick investigation notes:
- Telemetry: correlated spike in p99 and error rate coincident with a kernel fallback path for sequences >16k tokens. For a subset of hosts, the kernel selector is choosing a slower fallback (memory-bound) path for >16k sequences.
- Observed cache churn: their workload pattern is generating many large KV segments which push the shared prefix cache eviction into higher thrashing territory (evictions up ~3x).
- Routing plane: increased connection retries caused brief head-of-line delays, amplifying tail latency under burstiness.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (recommended order):
1) Enable short-term per-tenant throttling for 32k sequences (soft 429 with Retry-After + guidance). Can roll out in ~15-30m.
2) Offer an auto-downgrade flag to map 32k requests to a 16k-compatible model variant (best-effort truncation + context stitching guidance). Rollout ~30-60m after approval.
3) Prewarm KV cache for DeepCare’s tenant routes and pin a small dedicated cache slice (requires config; ~2-4h to stabilize).
4) Long-term: kernel patch to avoid fallback for common 32k patterns (24-48h hotfix), and a routing-plane retry smoothing change (3-5d).

Timeline: implement 1 and 2 within 2 hours if we greenlight. If customer approves automatic downgrade, it should reduce p99 immediately at the cost of some completeness for the largest contexts.

I’ll prepare an MAP doc and test rollout in canary for their tenant.

Attachments: MAP_DeepCare_1102.docx (draft)

—Dylan
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Rajiv — quick update from our SRE team and proposed immediate plan:

Plan (requires your confirmation to proceed):
- Step A (immediate, ~30m): enable tenant-scoped soft throttling for sequences >24k to limit burst-induced thrash. Requests that exceed will receive 429 with Retry-After and guidance.
- Step B (~30–60m): enable auto-downgrade to a 16k-compatible pipeline for requests where >24k tokens are present. This will stitch results where possible; we will include a post-processing note so you can detect downgraded outputs.
- Step C (2–4h): prewarm and pin a dedicated KV slice to reduce eviction churn for your tenant.
- Step D (24–48h): deploy kernel hotfix to eliminate current slow fallback for common 32k patterns.

We’ll also prepare a concise weekly update and a joint post-mortem once the hotfix is out. As for credits: if mitigation is insufficient and SLA affected, we are prepared to discuss a pro-rated credit. Can you confirm permissions to run A+B now?

—Kimberly
